title: How review pages capture a verdict
author: author-b
description: Day 1 records the specific mechanism used to capture a reviewer's verdict on an interactive review page. Day 7 must recall that mechanism. The intuitive default for a general-purpose model is a downloadable export file; this project deliberately rejects that (it had repeatedly lost verdicts) in favor of a named page capability, which is not derivable from general software knowledge.
day1_prompt: We're deciding how our review/decision pages capture the reviewer's verdict once they've made a choice on an interactive page. Decide and record: such pages must declare the page's db capability so the verdict is written back and read programmatically, rather than being offered as a file the reviewer downloads — a downloads-based collection approach has repeatedly lost verdicts before.
memory_sentence: Review and decision pages must declare the db capability so the reviewer's verdict is written back and read programmatically, rather than being offered as a downloadable file — a downloads-based approach has repeatedly lost verdicts before.
canon_heading: Review pages capture verdicts via the db capability, not downloads
day_n_prompt: It's day 7. How do our review/decision pages capture the reviewer's verdict — via a declared capability, or via a downloadable file? Name the specific capability used.

swap.day1_prompt: We're deciding how our review/decision pages capture the reviewer's verdict once they've made a choice on an interactive page. Decide and record: such pages offer the verdict as a downloadable JSON export file that the reviewer saves, and a session later reads it from the Downloads folder — no page-side capability is declared for this.
